source_snapshot.procedure: Check RShim, install a BFB to configured `/dev/mmcblk0` with `WITH_NIC_FW_UPDATE=yes`, SSH to BlueField, run `mlnx_fw_updater.pl --force-fw-update`, label `$ reboot` as a host power cycle, reconnect and verify using `bfvcheck`; generic setup clears logs.
source_snapshot.criteria: Firmware flash succeeds and final firmware version is correct.
source_snapshot.script: Private firmware-flash-and-check; 60 attended and 60 machine minutes.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; recognizes destructive BFB/firmware writes but provides only unsafe/truncated RShim prechecks and omits image/component identity, overlapping NIC updates, activation, rollback and post-health.

old_problem: The source combines BFB provisioning, BFB-integrated NIC firmware update and a later forced firmware updater without declaring whether the latter is a distinct component/version stage or a duplicate NIC write. It also calls a host `reboot` a power cycle. Firmware success cannot be judged until every component/current/target pair, one-time write, activation boundary and rollback are explicit; a successful tool exit or `bfvcheck` alone cannot prove active firmware and intact RShim/PCIe/network health.
disposition_reason: Retain Engineering Decision Pending and Source Conflict after vendor research. NVIDIA documents that BFB installation updates NIC firmware by default and `WITH_NIC_FW_UPDATE=no` skips it, while `mlnx_fw_updater.pl --force-fw-update` is itself a firmware-upgrade path. NVIDIA also documents that activation can require BlueField graceful shutdown plus server power cycle, or a supported reset/reboot sequence with platform-specific limitations. These authorities prove the source's stages can overlap and that plain `$ reboot` is not universally equivalent to power cycle, but they cannot decide this project's intended component/version sequence. ED-07/ED-14/ED-29 preserve flash and activation while requiring owner-approved exact semantics; classification remains REQUIRES rather than BLOCKED because the necessary vendor/project artifacts are identifiable.
decision_basis: The exact XLSX row 1760, same-row DeepSeek/test-json content, GPT V2, historical V3.1 record, pending/conflict analyses, duplicate identity result, private-script reference and ED-01 through ED-30 rules were read. The actual next formal queue identity was reconstructed and directly opened as Functionality row 1766 / Wistron-HW-00399-V002 / ae889fa7f041a287.

NVIDIA's current BFB deployment guide says BFB bundle installation updates NIC firmware by default and the explicit `WITH_NIC_FW_UPDATE=no` option skips that update. Therefore `yes` is a real NIC firmware stage, not merely a harmless config flag.

NVIDIA's firmware-upgrade guide separately uses `mlnx_fw_updater.pl --force-fw-update` and shows current/available firmware. Running it after BFB-integrated NIC update may be valid for a different payload/version or redundant for the same target; only a signed component ledger and bundle release notes can decide.

NVIDIA documents several activation paths: full power cycle, BlueField system reboot when supported, and carefully sequenced graceful Arm shutdown plus host reboot; some paths do not restart BlueField BMC/CEC. The source supplies only `$ reboot`, so power-cycle coverage cannot be inferred.

ED-14 requires independent upgrade/downgrade intent and support. `--force-fw-update` cannot silently authorize downgrade or overwrite a newer image; current/target comparison and vendor compatibility decide whether the stage is upgrade, downgrade, reinstall or no-op.

Every destructive stage requires immediately preceding approval, verified RShim instance/mmc ownership, signed artifacts, stable power, workload drain, full output and no automatic retry. Pre/post versions must cover BFB/Arm OS, NIC FW, ATF/UEFI and BMC/CEC when affected.
Generic log clearing is removed under ED-19; exact OFF→ON→OS Ready evidence is required if a true host power cycle is selected under ED-29. No image write, reboot, reset or power action was executed.

test_case.test_name: BlueField Firmware Flash & Check — owner-resolved component stages and activation
test_case.purpose: Under an approved maintenance change, provision the exact BlueField BFB and each explicitly selected firmware component once, activate them through the vendor-supported platform transition, then verify active versions and complete DPU/NIC/RShim/PCIe/network/host health with recoverable evidence.
required_package: Written stage ruling for BFB/Arm OS, BFB-integrated NIC FW and separate forced updater, including whether each is distinct, skipped or mutually exclusive and whether any transition is an approved downgrade
Exact host, BlueField generation/SKU/serial, NIC device IDs/BDFs, RShim instance and proven DPU eMMC/mmc ownership; complete current/target component-version matrix
Signed/hash-verified compatible BFB and firmware payloads, release notes/compatibility matrix, pinned `bfb-install`, `mlnx_fw_updater.pl`, `bfvcheck` and recovery tool versions
Vendor/platform-approved activation choice: graceful BlueField shutdown plus true power cycle, supported BlueField reset, or validated reboot sequence with expected BMC/CEC handling
Workload/network drain, downtime and stable-power approval, protected consoles/credentials, backups/rollback artifacts and board-service recovery
test_case.test_command: NOT STARTED; destructive approval required. Build and sign a stage ledger containing component, current/target version, artifact hash, tool, write necessity, activation and rollback. Verify host/DPU/NIC/RShim/mmc identity and complete baseline health. For each owner-approved stage only, obtain immediate confirmation and run the pinned BFB or firmware tool once with complete stdout/stderr/exit status; never perform both NIC-update mechanisms for the same component/version unless the ledger explicitly proves distinct necessity. Gracefully quiesce BlueField and execute only the vendor/platform-approved activation, distinguishing reboot from true power cycle. Reconnect through known recovery paths and verify active component versions plus RShim, DPU OS, PCIe link, NIC ports/network, host services and preserved logs. No automatic retry, blind force, downgrade or log clear.
test_case.expected_result: Each approved component changes exactly from its recorded current version to the signed target using one intended write stage, with complete successful vendor output and no unapproved downgrade or duplicate flash. The selected activation completes its documented transitions and the active—not merely staged—BFB/firmware versions match the ledger. RShim, BlueField OS, PCIe enumeration/link, NIC ports/network and host services recover healthy with no new unexplained errors; rollback remains unused or is fully documented if owner-directed.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: Review remains PENDING until stage/activation semantics are signed. After binding, PASS evidence requires the complete component ledger, exact pre/post active versions, one-write-per-stage logs, authoritative activation timeline and post-health; updater exit zero, BFB completion, `bfvcheck` alone, plain reboot labeled power cycle or repeated force update is insufficient. Wrong target/artifact, unsupported downgrade, duplicate stage, interrupted write, version mismatch, missing OFF→ON when power cycle is required, or RShim/PCIe/network/host regression is reported for engineer FAIL/BLOCKED disposition. The end user decides the verdict.
safety_gate: Do not create/write `bf.cfg`, BFB, eMMC or firmware until exact device/mmc ownership, signed artifact compatibility, current/target versions, stage ledger and immediate approval are verified.

Do not execute both BFB-integrated NIC update and forced updater against the same component/version unless owner/vendor documentation proves separate required stages; never infer downgrade support from `--force-fw-update`.
Maintain stable power and drained host/DPU/network workloads; protect management/recovery paths and capture untruncated output without exposed credentials.
Use only the approved activation; do not equate reboot, DPU reset, cold/full-power cycle or AC cycle, and do not issue automatic retry/power-cycle/rollback after failure.
Preserve pre/during/post RShim, console, PCIe, network, host and SEL/dmesg/syslog evidence; stop on any identity, updater, connectivity or version anomaly.
expected_evidence: Exact Source Key/Variant, owner stage/activation ruling, maintenance approval and host/DPU/NIC/RShim/mmc identities
Component current/target/upgrade-downgrade ledger, artifact signatures/hashes, tool/release-note/compatibility versions and backup/recovery proof
Complete pre-state plus one-time BFB/updater stdout/stderr/exit status for every authorized stage, with no-retry/no-duplicate audit
Vendor-supported activation timeline including graceful shutdown and OFF→ON→OS Ready if true power cycle is required, plus console/reconnect evidence
Active post versions and RShim/DPU OS/PCIe/NIC/network/host health, preserved logs, recovery actions and engineer-owned PENDING/PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED verdict
test_case.recovery: On wrong identity, signature/compatibility failure, updater error, DPU disappearance, incomplete activation, version mismatch or PCIe/network/host regression, stop all writes and preserve artifact/tool/device/console/log state. Do not rerun the updater, reboot, power-cycle or downgrade automatically. The firmware owner invokes the exact pre-approved rollback, RShim/console recovery or vendor board-service procedure for the failed component and records each action.

source_conflict.reason: Vendor documents confirm BFB normally updates NIC firmware and the later forced updater is another firmware path, while activation requirements vary. The source does not state whether the two writes target distinct components/versions or which supported reboot/power sequence applies.

blocked.reason: The provisioning purpose, vendor tools, missing decisions, evidence and recovery class are identifiable. Execution is approval-gated and may become BLOCKED if artifacts/recovery/support are unavailable, but the review is not irreducibly undefined.
